questions.scenario: While casting a post-tensioned transfer beam for a 32-storey commercial tower, the Authorized Signatory (AS) of the RGBC observes severe honeycombing and voiding around the anchor zone after formwork stripping. Instead of immediately alerting the project team, the site agent attempts to patch the voids using structural epoxy mortar without structural calculations or notification. Which statutory requirement has the RGBC violated under the Buildings Ordinance?
options: A. Section 9(5)(a) for failing to ensure that the site agent holds minimum TCP-T4 qualifications before executing structural patch repairs.
B. Section 9(5)(b) by failing to give continuous supervision to the works and failing to give immediate written notice to the Building Authority of a material defect.
C. Section 14(1) because patching structural voids requires a separate amendment plan submission and consent prior to stripping formwork.
D. Section 24(1) for failing to serve a demolition order upon the concrete subcontractor within 48 hours of discovering honeycombing.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 9(5)(b) & Section 40(2A)
questions.rationale: Under Section 9(5)(b) of the Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123), a Registered General Building Contractor (RGBC) must give continuous supervision to the carrying out of the building works and, if it becomes known to the contractor that any work has been carried out with a material divergence or defect, must immediately give written notice thereof to the Building Authority (BA). Concurrently, failing to report or rectifying without reporting constitutes an offence under Section 40(2A). Option A confuses TCP qualifications with the primary contractor statutory duty; Option C misidentifies patching as an amendment plan triggering Section 14(1); Option D incorrectly attributes the statutory demolition order power (vested exclusively in the BA under Section 24) to the contractor.

questions.scenario: The Building Authority granted consent under Section 16(1)(b) of the Buildings Ordinance for rock-socketed steel H-piling works subject to a condition under Section 17(1) requiring proof drilling into sound rock beneath 100% of the pile tips. Facing tight deadlines, the RGBC skips proof drilling on 6 out of 40 pile positions where core drill rigs could not fit, relying instead on adjacent geological borehole interpolations. What are the legal implications under the Ordinance?
options: A. The RGBC has committed a criminal offence under Section 40(2AA) for failing to comply with a condition imposed by the Building Authority under Section 17(1).
B. The RGBC is liable solely for civil liquidated damages to the developer under common law, as Section 17 conditions are technical advisories.
C. The works are automatically validated if the Registered Structural Engineer (RSE) signs a retroactive waiver on Form BA14.
D. The contractor is only subject to a minor statutory penalty if ground settlement exceeds 25 mm as prescribed in PNAP APP-24.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 17(1) & Section 40(2AA)
questions.rationale: Under Section 17(1) of the Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123), the Building Authority has statutory power to impose conditions when granting consent or approving plans, such as requiring proof drilling or load testing. Under Section 40(2AA), any person who fails to comply with any condition imposed under Section 17(1) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine at level 6 and to imprisonment for 2 years. Option B is false as Section 17 conditions are statutory mandates carrying criminal liability. Option C is invalid because an RSE has no statutory power to waive statutory conditions imposed by the BA. Option D is an arbitrary distraction.

questions.scenario: An RGBC received consent to carry out superstructure works on 5 March 2024. Due to a contractual dispute between the developer and main financier, no physical site operations commenced. On 20 June 2024, the dispute was settled and the RGBC plans to immediately commence casting the ground floor slab using the original consent. How does the Buildings Ordinance govern this situation?
options: A. The consent remains fully valid for 12 months from the date of grant under Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1).
B. The consent is deemed revoked under Section 20(1) because works were not commenced within 3 months, and the RGBC must apply for renewal under Section 20(2) on Form BA9.
C. The RGBC can commence immediately provided a Form BA10 is submitted 7 days prior to commencement pursuant to Section 14(1).
D. The consent is suspended under Section 23 and the RGBC must apply to the District Court for an injunction to restart.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 20(1) & (2); B(A)R Regulation 34; Form BA9
questions.rationale: Pursuant to Section 20(1) of the Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123), a consent given by the Building Authority to commence building works is deemed to be revoked if the works are not commenced within 3 months from the date of the consent, or if having commenced they are suspended for a period of 3 months. Because more than 3 months elapsed without commencement (5 March to 20 June), the consent was extinguished. To resume, an application for renewal of consent under Section 20(2) must be submitted using specified Form BA9 (together with prescribed fees and declarations under B(A)R Regulation 34). Option A refers to a non-existent 12-month rule. Option C is illegal because Form BA10 cannot revive an already revoked consent. Option D references cease-works orders inappropriately.

questions.scenario: Upon completion of a new 28-storey hotel, the AP and RGBC apply to the Building Authority for an Occupation Permit (OP) under Section 21 of the Buildings Ordinance. During the inspection, the BA discovers that the fire-resisting doors protecting the central escape staircases are missing their statutory certifiable test reports and do not comply with the approved plans, posing an egress hazard. On which statutory ground must the BA refuse the OP?
options: A. Section 21(6)(a), because the building owner has failed to pay the standard inspection fee prescribed in B(A)R Reg. 42.
B. Section 21(6)(d), because the building works have not been completed in accordance with the provisions of the Buildings Ordinance or the approved plans in a material manner.
C. Section 21(4), because an RGBC is not permitted to apply for an OP unless a certificate of structural stability has been issued by the Fire Services Department.
D. Section 23(1), because the Building Authority is compelled to issue a Cease Works Order on completed buildings.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 21(6)(d)
questions.rationale: Under Section 21(6)(d) of the Buildings Ordinance, the Building Authority may refuse to issue an occupation permit if the building has not been completed in accordance with the provisions of the Ordinance or approved plans, or if there is material non-compliance affecting life safety or statutory standards. Fire separation in protected exit routes is a core requirement of the approved plans and Building (Planning) Regulations / Fire Safety Code. Option A is a fabricated procedural barrier; Option C misallocates statutory duties, as FSD issues Fire Services Certificates (F.S. 172), not certificates of structural stability; Option D confuses post-completion refusal under Section 21 with stop-work powers under Section 23.

questions.scenario: During open trench excavation for external drainage adjoining a busy public pedestrian pavement, the contractor's unbraced cut slips, causing 60 mm of lateral ground displacement, tearing an active gas main, and fracturing the water main beneath the street. The Building Authority conducts an emergency inspection. Which statutory order is the Building Authority empowered to serve immediately under Section 23 of the Buildings Ordinance?
options: A. An order in writing requiring that the building works or such part thereof as is specified in the order be ceased forthwith until the danger is removed.
B. A mandatory demolition order requiring the demolition of the entire building development within 7 days.
C. A closure order under Section 24A directed to the Director of Highways to close the public road permanently.
D. A disciplinary summons requiring the immediate surrender of the RGBC's registration certificate without hearing.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 23(1) & (2)
questions.rationale: Under Section 23(1) of the Buildings Ordinance, where building works are being carried out in such a manner as to cause or to be likely to cause a risk of injury to any person or damage to any property, the Building Authority may by order in writing require that the building works, or such part thereof as is specified in the order, shall cease forthwith. Option B (Section 24) concerns unauthorized structures, not emergency stoppage of dangerous ongoing operations. Option C confuses Section 24A (which applies to dangerous buildings/structures, requiring District Court application) with Section 23 powers. Option D misstates Section 13 disciplinary proceedings, which require a Disciplinary Board hearing.

questions.scenario: An RGBC executing structural alteration and addition (A&A) works on the 4th floor of an industrial building discovers that the owner previously erected an extensive unauthorized reinforced concrete mezzanine floor on the 2nd floor that is heavily overloaded and exhibiting wide structural shear cracks. The BA serves a notice under Section 24(1). What is the exact statutory scope of an order under Section 24(1) of the Buildings Ordinance?
options: A. An order requiring the contractor to construct underpinning piles within 24 hours at the contractor's own expense.
B. An order requiring the demolition of the building works, or such alteration or rectification as may be necessary to bring the works into conformity with the Ordinance.
C. An order automatically transferring ownership of the industrial building to the Government of Hong Kong under Crown land resumption terms.
D. A custodial detention warrant against the Authorized Signatory issued directly by the Chief Building Surveyor.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 24(1)
questions.rationale: Section 24(1) of the Buildings Ordinance empowers the Building Authority, where any building has been erected or building works have been carried out in contravention of any provision of the Ordinance, to serve a notice/order in writing requiring the demolition of the building works or such alteration or rectification as may be necessary to bring them into conformity with the Ordinance or approved plans. Options A, C, and D are legally baseless powers not found in Section 24.

questions.scenario: During an excavation next to an pre-war residential tenement, improper dewatering induces severe differential settlement, causing the tenement wall to bulge outward by 120 mm with deep diagonal masonry fractures. The BA determines the tenement is in a state of imminent collapse, posing immediate danger to the occupants. Which statutory power must the Building Authority deploy to exclude occupants and protect life?
options: A. Issue a summons under Section 40(2A) ordering the tenants to perform underpinning works.
B. Apply to the District Court for a Closure Order under Section 24A and, if urgent, serve a notice of intention and exercise emergency closure powers.
C. Issue an immediate Section 20(1) notice revoking the tenement's original 1950 occupation permit.
D. Instruct the Fire Services Department to seize the land under the Police Force Ordinance.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 24A
questions.rationale: Under Section 24A of the Buildings Ordinance, where the Building Authority considers that any building is in a dangerous condition, application may be made to the District Court for a Closure Order to close the building and exclude occupants to avert danger to life. In circumstances of imminent danger, the BA can serve notice and secure the premises. Option A misapplies criminal penalty provisions to occupants; Option C is invalid as Section 20(1) applies to consents for works, not occupation permits; Option D cites irrelevant ordinances.

questions.scenario: An RGBC's Authorized Signatory submits Specified Form BA14 (Certificate of Completion of Building Works) to the Building Authority, falsely certifying that all high-tensile steel reinforcement bars used in the foundation columns were sourced from BD-approved mills with valid mill certificates, knowing full well that uncertified rebar of questionable origin was used to overcome supply delays. Under which statutory provision is the AS personally subject to severe criminal liability?
options: A. Section 40(1AA), which criminalizes knowingly making any false representation or statement in any document submitted to the Building Authority.
B. Section 13(1), which allows the Magistrate to sentence the AS directly to 10 years imprisonment without a criminal trial.
C. Section 28(3), for discharging unapproved wastewater into public storm drains.
D. Section 42, which grants absolute immunity to any registered contractor submitting specified statutory forms in good faith.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 40(1AA)
questions.rationale: Section 40(1AA) of the Buildings Ordinance specifies that any person who knowingly makes any false representation or false statement in any plan, certificate, form or other document submitted to the Building Authority under the Ordinance commits a criminal offence. Upon conviction on indictment, the maximum penalty is a fine of HK$1,000,000 and imprisonment for 3 years. Option B confuses Disciplinary Boards under Section 13 (which have civil/administrative disciplinary powers, not custodial sentencing) with criminal courts; Option C covers drainage; Option D describes an entirely fictitious immunity.

questions.scenario: To cut construction costs during basement construction, an RGBC's site manager deliberately eliminates two levels of steel walers and struts shown on the approved Excavation and Lateral Support (ELS) plans without obtaining prior approval or consent. The sheet-pile wall collapses into the excavation, crushing an adjacent access road and severely injuring two municipal utility workers. Under which section will the RGBC and its AS be criminally prosecuted for causing personal injury and property damage?
options: A. Section 40(2B)(b), for carrying out works in a manner that causes or is likely to cause risk of injury to any person or damage to any property.
B. Section 40(1), for failing to display the contractor's registration certificate on the site entrance hoarding.
C. Section 24(2), for failing to provide an indemnity bond to the Director of Lands.
D. Section 16(3), for commencing works on a statutory public holiday.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 40(2B)(b)
questions.rationale: Section 40(2B)(b) of the Buildings Ordinance creates a serious criminal offence where any person carrying out or directly concerned with the carrying out of any building works carries out those works in such a manner as to cause or to be likely to cause a risk of injury to any person or damage to any property. The penalty on conviction on indictment is a fine of HK$1,000,000 and imprisonment for 3 years. Options B, C, and D cite inapplicable or distorted administrative clauses.

questions.scenario: An RGBC is convicted in the Magistrates' Court under Section 40(2A) of the Buildings Ordinance for carrying out structural transfer plate works with material divergence from approved plans. The Building Authority brings the conviction before a Contractors Disciplinary Board appointed under Section 13. Which of the following orders is legally within the statutory jurisdiction of the Disciplinary Board?
options: A. Sentencing the Authorized Signatory to 6 months imprisonment and ordering immediate remand in custody.
B. Ordering that the name of the contractor or AS be removed from the register, or reprimanding them, or fining them up to the statutory limit.
C. Directing the Hong Kong Police Force to confiscate the contractor's corporate bank accounts and heavy machinery.
D. Issuing a permanent injunction restraining the contractor from operating any commercial enterprise in Hong Kong.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 13(4) & (4A)
questions.rationale: Under Section 13(4) of the Buildings Ordinance, a Disciplinary Board has statutory powers upon inquiry to: (a) order that the name of the contractor or its Authorized Signatory/director be removed from the register (either permanently or for a specified period); (b) reprimand the contractor or person; or (c) fine the contractor/person an amount not exceeding HK$250,000 (Section 13(4A)). Disciplinary Boards are administrative tribunals and do NOT possess powers of custodial sentencing (imprisonment, Option A), asset forfeiture (Option C), or general commercial injunctions (Option D), which reside solely with the judicial courts.

questions.scenario: A property developer terminates the incumbent main contractor during ongoing superstructure works due to commercial insolvency and formally retains a new RGBC to assume immediate control of the site. The developer instructs the incoming RGBC's Authorized Signatory (AS) to take over construction operations immediately on site while paperwork is sorted out over the following weeks.
options: A. The incoming RGBC may proceed with superstructure works immediately, provided Form BA8 is submitted to the Building Authority within 14 days of taking over site possession.

B. Under Building (Administration) Regulation 8(1), notice of appointment of the new RGBC must be given on Form BA8 within 7 days of appointment, and works cannot lawfully proceed under the new RGBC until the appointment is formally executed and recognized by the Building Authority.
C. The incoming RGBC must re-apply for full plan approval under Section 14(1) of the Buildings Ordinance before submitting Form BA8.
D. The developer and the outgoing contractor can unilaterally endorse a deed of assignment, exempting the incoming RGBC from submitting Form BA8 provided a new Form BA10 is logged.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulation 8(1) & (2); Form BA8; Buildings Ordinance Section 9(5)
questions.rationale: Under Building (Administration) Regulation 8(1), notice of the appointment of a registered contractor shall be given to the Building Authority in the specified form (Form BA8) within 7 days of the appointment. Under BO Section 9(5) and Section 14(1), an RGBC cannot lawfully execute building works on site without a valid statutory appointment and consent recognized by the Building Authority. Carrying out works without valid contractor registration/appointment is an offence under BO Section 40(2A). Option A is incorrect because the statutory deadline is 7 days, not 14 days, and works cannot proceed unlawfully. Options C and D are legally baseless.

questions.scenario: An RGBC holding a valid consent to construct a private hospital halts all site works on 1 February due to a severe contractual dispute between the main contractor and employer. The dispute is settled and the site is handed back on 20 June (an inactive stoppage period of 4 months and 20 days), whereupon the project director orders the immediate pouring of basement slabs on 21 June.
options: A. Works may resume immediately because the original consent remains valid for 24 months from the date of initial issuance by the Building Authority.

B. Under Section 20(1) of the Buildings Ordinance, the consent is deemed revoked because works were suspended for more than 3 months; the RGBC must apply for and obtain renewal of consent using Form BA9 under B(A)R Regulation 34 before resuming any building works.
C. The RGBC may resume works immediately provided an explanatory letter is submitted to the Building Authority under repealed B(A)R Regulation 27 within 48 hours.
D. The consent remains valid provided the Authorized Person issues a site instruction confirming the structural integrity of the temporary shoring has not degraded.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 20(1) & 20(2); Building (Administration) Regulation 34; Form BA9
questions.rationale: Under Section 20(1) of the Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123), any consent given by the Building Authority shall be deemed to be revoked if the building works are not commenced within 3 months, or if commenced, are suspended for a period of more than 3 months. Because the suspension exceeded 3 months, the consent was revoked by operation of law. Resuming work without renewed consent constitutes carrying out works without consent under BO Section 14(1), an offence under Section 40(1AA). Renewal must be applied for under BO Section 20(2) using Form BA9 pursuant to B(A)R Regulation 34. B(A)R Regulation 27 was repealed and has no legal force.

questions.scenario: On 2 May, the Building Authority issues formal consent for the construction of a deep basement excavation and lateral support system. The employer demands that the RGBC start driving sheet piles on 6 May to meet contractual milestones, and the RGBC AS submits Form BA10 on 3 May specifying 6 May as the commencement date.
options: A. Commencing works on 6 May complies with the law because Form BA10 was submitted prior to the physical commencement of works.

B. Commencing works on 6 May violates Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1), which requires the RGBC to give not less than 7 days' advance notice of commencement on Form BA10 to the Building Authority.
C. The RGBC may proceed on 6 May if the Registered Geotechnical Engineer gives verbal concurrence to the advance commencement.
D. Form BA10 is only required for superstructure works, whereas deep excavation works require only a site log entry under the Site Safety Supervision Plan.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1); Form BA10; Buildings Ordinance Section 40(2A)
questions.rationale: Under Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1), an RGBC to whom consent has been given must give not less than 7 days' notice of the intended date of commencement in the specified form (Form BA10) to the Building Authority. Submitting Form BA10 on 3 May for a 6 May commencement provides only 3 days' notice, directly breaching Reg 20(1). Any commencement prior to the expiry of the mandatory 7-day period renders the RGBC and AS liable to statutory penalties under BO Section 40(2A).

questions.scenario: A 35-storey commercial office development reaches practical completion. The developer is eager to hand over tenant spaces and pressures the RGBC AS to sign Form BA14 immediately, despite knowing that mandatory fire-rated drywall partitions enclosing several electrical riser ducts have been omitted to facilitate late cabling works.
options: A. The RGBC AS may lawfully sign Form BA14 provided the omission is noted as a contractor punch-list item to be rectified prior to tenant occupation.
B. The RGBC AS may sign Form BA14 only if the Authorized Person concurrently submits an application for a Temporary Occupation Permit on Form BA13.

C. Signing Form BA14 while knowing that works deviate materially from the approved plans is a criminal offence under Section 40(2A) and Section 40(2AE) of the Buildings Ordinance, subjecting the AS to a maximum fine of HK$1,000,000 and 3 years' imprisonment.
D. Form BA14 only certifies structural stability, whereas fire-rated compartmentalization is strictly certified by the Fire Services Department on Form FSI/314.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulation 25(1); Specified Form BA14; Buildings Ordinance Section 40(2A) & Section 40(2AE)
questions.rationale: On Form BA14 (Certificate of Completion of Building Works), the RGBC AS certifies that the building works have been completed in accordance with the provisions of the Buildings Ordinance and the approved plans. Knowingly certifying completion when mandatory fire-rated enclosures have been deliberately omitted constitutes knowingly making a material misrepresentation or false statement to the Building Authority. Under BO Section 40(2A) and Section 40(2AE), an AS who makes an incorrect/false certificate commits a serious criminal offence punishable by a HK$1,000,000 fine and 3 years' imprisonment, in addition to disciplinary action under BO Section 13.

questions.scenario: A multi-storey shopping mall project includes extensive specialized mechanical ventilation and smoke extraction systems executed by an appointed Registered Specialist Contractor in the Ventilation Works category [RSC(V)]. The project team is assembling the statutory completion package for submission to the Building Authority to obtain an Occupation Permit under Section 21 of the Buildings Ordinance.
options: A. The RSC(V) is not required to sign any statutory Building Authority form, as the ventilation system is covered exclusively by Fire Services Department Form FSI/314.
B. The RGBC AS must certify all mechanical ventilation works on Form BA14, with the RSC(V) signing merely as an internal commercial subcontractor.

C. Under Building (Administration) Regulation 25(2), the RSC(V) must execute and submit Form BA14A to certify completion of the specialized ventilation works, which accompanies the RGBC's Form BA14 and the AP's Form BA12.
D. Form BA14A is only required for foundation and ground investigation works, whereas ventilation systems require Form BA15.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulation 25(2); Specified Form BA14A; Buildings Ordinance Section 21
questions.rationale: Under Building (Administration) Regulation 25(2), where specialized works (such as ventilation works, foundation works, or ground investigation field works) have been carried out by a Registered Specialist Contractor (RSC), that RSC must sign a certificate in the specified form (Form BA14A) certifying that the specialist works have been carried out in accordance with the approved plans and statutory regulations. This Form BA14A must accompany the RGBC's Form BA14 and the AP's Form BA12 (application for Occupation Permit) submitted under BO Section 21.

questions.scenario: A building owner appoints an Authorized Person (AP) and an RGBC to carry out Class I Minor Works involving the construction of an internal reinforced concrete staircase connecting two retail floors. The RGBC AS is establishing the statutory submission program under the Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N).
options: A. The AP and RGBC must submit Form MW01 with prescribed plans at least 7 days before commencement, and submit Form MW02 with completion photos within 14 days after completion.
B. Class I Minor Works do not require prior notice; only Form MW02 must be submitted within 28 days after completion.
C. The RGBC must submit Form MW03 at least 14 days prior to commencement and Form MW04 within 7 days after completion.
D. Because the works involve reinforced concrete, the project cannot proceed under MWCS and requires full consent under Form BA10.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Sections 27, 28 & 29; Specified Forms MW01 & MW02
questions.rationale: Under Sections 27 and 28 of the Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N), for Class I Minor Works, the Prescribed Building Professional (AP/RSE) and the Prescribed Registered Contractor (RGBC) must submit a notice of commencement in Form MW01 together with prescribed plans and supervision plans at least 7 days before commencement. Under Section 29, within 14 days after physical completion, they must submit a certificate of completion in Form MW02 accompanied by record plans and photographs taken before, during, and after completion. Forming an internal staircase meeting Class I criteria (Item 1.1) is explicitly permitted under Schedule 1 of Cap. 123N.

questions.scenario: An incorporated owners' committee engages an RGBC directly to carry out Class II Minor Works (repair of external rendering and cladding exceeding 3m in height) where no Prescribed Building Professional (PBP) is statutorily required or appointed. The RGBC AS must properly comply with the commencement and completion filing requirements under Cap. 123N.
options: A. The RGBC must submit Form MW01 at least 7 days prior to commencement and Form MW06 within 14 days after completion.
B. The RGBC must submit Form MW03 at least 7 days before commencing the works, and submit Form MW06 (Notice of completion without a PBP) within 14 days after completion.
C. The RGBC must submit Form MW03 at least 14 days prior to commencement and Form MW04 within 21 days after completion.
D. No prior notice is required for Class II works without a PBP; the RGBC submits only Form MW05 within 14 days of completion.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Sections 30 & 32; Specified Forms MW03 & MW06
questions.rationale: Under B(MW)R Section 30, for Class II Minor Works, the contractor must submit a notice of commencement in Form MW03 at least 7 days before commencement. Under B(MW)R Section 32, where no Prescribed Building Professional is appointed for Class II works, the contractor must submit a notice of completion in Form MW06 within 14 days after completion. Form MW04 is used for Class II completion ONLY when a PBP is appointed, whereas Form MW05 is exclusively for Class III works.

questions.scenario: A homeowner engages an RGBC to install a standard projecting metal drying rack extending 700mm from the external wall of an 8th-floor flat, categorized as Class III Minor Works (Item 3.1). The client asks the RGBC AS on what date the Buildings Department will issue a commencement consent so drilling can begin.
options: A. Drilling may only start after the Buildings Department grants consent within 28 days of receiving Form MW05.
B. The RGBC must submit Form MW03 at least 7 days prior to drilling, and the consent is deemed granted if no objection is received.

C. Under the simplified Class III procedure in Section 35 of Cap. 123N, no prior notification or consent is required before commencing work; the RGBC must simply submit Form MW05 with record photos within 14 days after completion.
D. Because the rack is above ground level, the works are automatically upgraded to Class I requiring an AP and Form MW01.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Section 35; Specified Form MW05
questions.rationale: Under Section 35 of the Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N), Class III minor works do not require any prior notification or consent before commencement. They operate entirely under a post-completion reporting mechanism where the Prescribed Registered Contractor must submit a notice of completion on Form MW05, together with photos of the works before and after completion, within 14 days after completion.

questions.scenario: A commercial retail tenant engages an RGBC to cut an opening measuring 2.6m by 2.2m (total area 5.72 m²) in a reinforced concrete suspended floor slab for an internal display chute. The tenant's designer proposes filing this under the Minor Works Control System as Class I Minor Works Item 1.14.
options: A. The RGBC AS may accept the appointment under MWCS provided an Authorized Person and Registered Structural Engineer prepare the design on Form MW01.

B. The proposed slab opening exceeds the statutory dimensional threshold for Class I Minor Works (maximum slab opening area not exceeding 4.5 m²); therefore, it cannot be executed under MWCS and requires full formal plan submission and consent under Section 14(1) of the Buildings Ordinance.
C. The opening can be executed under Class II Minor Works using Form MW03 if temporary steel propping is installed underneath.
D. Any opening in a suspended slab is classified as an exempted work under Section 41(3) provided no primary structural beams are cut.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Schedule 1, Part 2, Item 1.14; Buildings Ordinance Section 14(1) & Section 40(1AA)
questions.rationale: Under Schedule 1, Part 2, Item 1.14 of the Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N), the formation of an opening in a suspended reinforced concrete floor slab under Class I Minor Works is strictly capped at an area not exceeding 4.5 m² (with no structural framing beam cut). Because the proposed opening is 5.72 m², it exceeds the statutory criteria and falls entirely outside the Minor Works Control System. Proceeding under MWCS would constitute carrying out unauthorized building works without formal approval and consent under BO Section 14(1), exposing the RGBC AS to prosecution under Section 40(1AA).

questions.scenario: An RGBC acting as the Prescribed Registered Contractor for Class I Minor Works completes an alteration to an external wall opening. To save time and avoid photographic evidence of non-compliant anchorage details, the RGBC AS submits Form MW02 to the Buildings Department with fabricated pre-construction photos and falsely certifies that the works comply fully with the submitted plans and statutory regulations.
options: A. Non-compliance on MWCS completion forms is an administrative matter dealt with exclusively via a Buildings Department warning letter.

B. Under Section 41 of the Building (Minor Works) Regulation and Section 40(2A) / 40(2AE) of the Buildings Ordinance, knowingly making a false representation or submitting a false certificate to the Building Authority is a criminal offence punishable by a fine up to HK$1,000,000 and 3 years' imprisonment, plus contractor disciplinary action.
C. The AS is immune from personal criminal liability because Form MW02 is co-signed by the Prescribed Building Professional.
D. Falsifying completion photos on Form MW02 carries a fixed penalty of HK$5,000 under the Simplified Minor Works Enforcement Scheme.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Sections 37 & 41; Buildings Ordinance Section 40(2A), Section 40(2AE) & Section 13
questions.rationale: Under B(MW)R Section 37, a prescribed registered contractor has a statutory duty to ensure minor works are executed in accordance with the Ordinance and to certify completion truthfully. Under B(MW)R Section 41 and BO Section 40(2A)/(2AE), any person who knowingly makes any false representation or signs any false certificate/document to the Building Authority commits a serious criminal offence, subject to a fine of HK$1,000,000 and 3 years' imprisonment. The AS and the RGBC are also subject to disciplinary proceedings under BO Section 13, which may result in fine, reprimand, or deregistration.

questions.scenario: During an unannounced site audit on an ongoing commercial tower construction, Buildings Department (BD) officers discover that the certified physical copies of the approved architectural and structural plans are kept at the RGBC's head office across town for safekeeping. The site office only maintains digital PDF drawings on tablet computers and unapproved structural steel fabrication shop drawings. The Authorized Signatory (AS) argues that high-resolution digital tablets fulfill statutory documentation requirements.
options: A. The AS is correct, as the Electronic Transactions Ordinance legally substitutes digital plan displays on tablets for physical approved drawings on construction sites.

B. The RGBC is in direct contravention of Building (Administration) Regulation 10, which mandates that certified copies of approved plans and documents must be kept constantly on the site during work execution.
C. The RGBC is compliant provided the Authorized Person (AP) has signed a formal letter delegating offsite plan custody to the contractor's head office.
D. The absence of approved plans on site is solely the statutory liability of the AP under Building (Administration) Regulation 6, exempting the RGBC from legal penalty.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulations (Cap. 123A) Regulation 10 & Buildings Ordinance Section 40(2B)
questions.rationale: Building (Administration) Regulation 10 explicitly mandates that the registered contractor shall keep on the site of building works a copy of the plans approved by the Building Authority, together with related approval letters and supervision documents. Maintaining copies offsite or relying solely on unapproved fabrication drawings or tablets without certified approved site sets constitutes a direct contravention, rendering the contractor liable to prosecution under Section 40(2B) of the Buildings Ordinance.

questions.scenario: Nine months after the issuance of an Occupation Permit for a 28-storey hotel development, the Building Authority conducts a forensic investigation into alleged substandard concrete batching and requests the RGBC to produce all site batching tickets, concrete cube crushing strength certificates, and contractor supervisory logbooks. The RGBC's management refuses, stating that the project has reached final financial settlement and that all site records were shredded six months post-occupation.
options: A. The RGBC is legally entitled to dispose of quality records upon issuance of the Occupation Permit, as statutory retention duties expire on practical completion.

B. The RGBC has contravened Building (Administration) Regulation 11, which obligates the registered contractor to retain all test records and supervisory logs for at least 12 months after completion of the works.
C. The RGBC is exempt from liability if the independent testing laboratory holds digital duplicates of the crushing records for three years.
D. Test records must only be retained by the Registered Structural Engineer (RSE); contractors have no statutory retention duty under Cap. 123A.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulations (Cap. 123A) Regulation 11 & Buildings Ordinance Section 40(2A)
questions.rationale: Under Building (Administration) Regulation 11, every registered contractor must preserve and keep all records of tests carried out on building materials, supervisory logbooks, and related inspection documents for a minimum period of not less than 12 months after the completion of the works (or expiry of consent). Premature destruction within 9 months post-completion constitutes a criminal contravention under Section 40(2A) of the Buildings Ordinance.

questions.scenario: The Building Authority issues formal consent to commence foundation works for a new residential development. On Monday morning, the RGBC delivers Specified Form BA10 (Notice of Commencement) to the Buildings Department, nominating the coming Friday (4 calendar days later) as the commencement date, and immediately mobilizes heavy hydraulic drilling rigs to execute preliminary working piles on Friday morning.
options: A. The commencement is valid because the receipt of Form BA10 by BD automatically waives the statutory notice period for foundation works.

B. The works executed on Friday constitute unauthorized commencement under Section 14(1) and a breach of Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1), which requires not less than 7 days' prior notice before commencing works.
C. The RGBC may commence after 48 hours provided the Authorized Person countersigns Form BA10 confirming urgent ground stabilization.
D. The notice period under Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1) is exactly 3 working days excluding public holidays.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulations (Cap. 123A) Regulation 20(1) & Buildings Ordinance Section 14(1), 40(2A)
questions.rationale: Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1) strictly provides that a registered contractor must give not less than 7 days' prior written notice in the specified form (Form BA10) to the Building Authority before commencing building works. Mobilizing and drilling on Day 4 breaches this statutory minimum period, rendering the operations premature and legally unauthorized under Sections 14(1) and 40(2A).

questions.scenario: An RGBC obtained consent from the Building Authority to commence superstructure works on 15 January. Due to prolonged commercial disputes with the employer, no physical site works commenced. On 20 May (more than 4 months later), the disputes are resolved and the RGBC prepares to commence construction immediately by serving Form BA10, claiming that the original consent remains fully active until structural works finish.
options: A. The consent remains valid indefinitely as long as the approved plans have not been revoked or superseded.

B. The consent is deemed revoked under Section 20(1) of the Buildings Ordinance because works were not commenced within 3 months of its grant; the RGBC must apply for renewal under Section 20(2) / B(A)R Regulation 34 using Form BA9 before serving Form BA10.
C. Under Building (Administration) Regulation 27, the RGBC may unilaterally extend the consent by giving a 14-day notice to the Building Authority.
D. The consent is valid for 6 months for superstructure works, allowing commencement up to 15 July without any renewal.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 20(1) & (2); Building (Administration) Regulations Regulation 34 & Form BA9
questions.rationale: Pursuant to Section 20(1) of the Buildings Ordinance, a consent to commence building works is deemed to be revoked if the work is not commenced within 3 months from the date of the grant of consent. To revive it, an application for consent renewal must be submitted under Section 20(2) using Form BA9, and endorsed by the Building Authority under B(A)R Regulation 34. Commencing works on a lapsed consent without renewal violates Section 14(1). (Note: B(A)R Regulation 27 is repealed).

questions.scenario: During the tensioning and locking-off of unbonded post-tensioned tendons on a complex 40-metre transfer plate, BD officers inspect the site and find that the RGBC's Authorized Signatory and all contractor Technically Competent Persons (TCPs) are absent at a corporate seminar offsite. The stressing operations are being directed entirely by an uncertified sub-contractor trade foreman. The RGBC claims continuous supervision only applies during concrete casting.
options: A. Prestressing stressing operations do not require contractor supervision if the pre-pour concrete cube results have achieved target strength.

B. Building (Administration) Regulation 26 requires the registered contractor to provide continuous supervision of the carrying out of building works by an authorized signatory or competent representative, making absence during critical operations a direct regulatory contravention.
C. Continuous supervision is exclusively the statutory responsibility of the Registered Structural Engineer's stream TCPs under the SSPS Code.
D. The contractor is only required to maintain periodic supervision, defined as a minimum of one site inspection per calendar week.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulations (Cap. 123A) Regulation 26 & Buildings Ordinance Section 9(5)(a)
questions.rationale: Building (Administration) Regulation 26 imposes a non-delegable duty on the registered contractor to provide continuous supervision during the execution of building works by an authorized signatory or a designated competent person. Abandoning critical, high-risk structural operations such as post-tensioning without qualified supervisory personnel contravenes Reg. 26 and Section 9(5)(a) of the Buildings Ordinance.

questions.scenario: To facilitate facade cleaning and cladding installation on a dense commercial street, an RGBC erects a temporary hoarding and covered walkway over the public pavement. Due to site constraints caused by an adjacent street tree, the RGBC designs the covered walkway with a clear walking width of 0.95 metres and an internal clear headroom of 2.25 metres. The AP asks the RGBC whether this meets BD requirements under PNRC 4.
options: A. The dimensions are acceptable as long as emergency lighting and warning stripes are installed at both ends.

B. The walkway contravenes PNRC 4 and Building (Planning) Regulations standards, which stipulate a minimum clear width of not less than 1.1 metres (unless the pavement itself is narrower) and a minimum clear headroom of not less than 2.5 metres.
C. Clear headroom of 2.25 metres is permitted for covered walkways provided the clear width is maintained at 1.0 metre.
D. Temporary hoardings and walkways are strictly governed by the Highways Department; the Buildings Department has no statutory jurisdiction over pedestrian dimensions.
questions.statutoryRef: Practice Note for Registered Contractors PNRC 4 (Appendix A) & Building (Planning) Regulations (Cap. 123F) Regulation 49
questions.rationale: Under Practice Note for Registered Contractors PNRC 4 (Appendix A) and B(P)R Regulation 49, covered walkways erected over public pavements must provide a minimum clear walking width of 1.1 m (or matching full pavement width if narrower) and an unobstructed vertical clear headroom of not less than 2.5 m. A width of 0.95 m and headroom of 2.25 m fail these explicit safety and circulation standards.

questions.scenario: An RGBC is executing open-cut basement excavation within the Railway Protection Zone of an operational MTR underground tunnel. The agreed geotechnical instrumentation monitoring plan stipulates an Alert level of 15mm, an Alarm level of 18mm, and an Action / Suspension level of 20mm total movement. During excavation, automated railway prism sensors record 21.5mm of cumulative lateral tunnel displacement.
options: A. The RGBC may continue excavation at a reduced rate while recalculating the Finite Element geotechnical model over the next 7 days.

B. Under PNRC 14 (APP-24) and Section 17(1) of the Buildings Ordinance, the RGBC must immediately cease all excavation works affecting the railway, notify the Building Authority and MTR Corporation, and implement emergency mitigation measures.
C. The contractor only needs to halt works if the Registered Geotechnical Engineer (RGE) is served with a formal stop order by the Director of Fire Services.
D. Exceeding 20mm is classified as a minor anomaly that merely requires the contractor to increase surveying frequency from daily to hourly without stopping excavation.
questions.statutoryRef: Practice Note for Registered Contractors PNRC 14 (APP-24) & Buildings Ordinance Section 17(1)(a)
questions.rationale: Under PNRC 14 (PNAP APP-24) and standard consent conditions imposed under Section 17(1) of the Buildings Ordinance, when structural displacement or ground settlement reaches the trigger level (commonly 20mm in the Railway Protection Zone), all works contributing to the movement must be suspended immediately. The RGBC and AP/RSE must immediately inform BD and MTRCL and execute pre-approved remedial contingency measures.

questions.scenario: A specialist piling company registered as an RGBC has only one Authorized Signatory (AS) listed on the BD register. While critical bored piling works are halfway through concreting beneath the water table, the sole AS resigns abruptly following an internal shareholder dispute and notifies BD. The RGBC's board appoints an experienced Project Director (holding a civil engineering degree and 20 years' site experience) to oversee operations and continue concreting.
options: A. The Project Director may act as de facto AS for up to 28 days under PNRC 38 while a new AS application is processed by BD.

B. All building works on site must immediately cease upon the cessation of employment of the sole AS, as the RGBC lacks legal authorization to carry out works under Buildings Ordinance Section 9(5) and PNRC 38.
C. Concreting may continue indefinitely provided the Registered Structural Engineer (RSE) provides full-time resident supervision on site.
D. The contractor may continue works without an AS provided Form BA10 was submitted prior to the AS's resignation date.
questions.statutoryRef: Practice Note for Registered Contractors PNRC 38 Section 4 & Buildings Ordinance Section 9(5), 9(6)
questions.rationale: Under PNRC 38 Section 4 and Buildings Ordinance Section 9(5) & 9(6), an RGBC cannot lawfully execute building works without an approved Authorized Signatory acting on its behalf. When the sole AS resigns or ceases to act, the contractor must immediately cease all building works. Appointing an internal Project Director without prior BD registration and approval is illegal.

questions.scenario: During the construction of a 4-storey commercial podium, the RGBC and developer decide to delete an internal double-height architectural void to create 450 m² of additional retail floor space, and to substantially increase the structural design dead loads on the supporting transfer columns. The AS advises the employer that this modification can be handled as 'minor amendments' and reported to BD upon completion on Form BA14.
options: A. The AS's advice is correct under PNAP APP-55, as any internal slab addition within an existing building envelope is deemed non-material.

B. The AS's advice violates PNAP APP-55 / PNRC 52 and Section 14(1) of the Buildings Ordinance, because modifications that increase gross floor area (GFA), site coverage, or structural load paths cannot be treated as minor amendments and strictly require prior plan approval and consent.
C. The contractor may proceed with construction as long as the Registered Structural Engineer confirms the columns have adequate structural reserve capacity.
D. Retail floor space additions are exempted from prior approval under the Building (Minor Works) Regulation.
questions.statutoryRef: PNAP APP-55 / PNRC 52 & Buildings Ordinance Section 14(1), Section 40(2A)
questions.rationale: Under PNAP APP-55 and PNRC 52, the simplified minor amendment procedure applies strictly to non-material structural/architectural variations that do not affect structural stability, overall building envelope, or town planning restrictions. Any amendment that increases Gross Floor Area (GFA), site coverage, or imposes substantial new structural loads strictly requires formal prior plan submission, approval, and consent under Section 14(1) before execution.

questions.scenario: On a complex deep foundation and excavation site, the TCP T3 representative of the Registered Structural Engineer (RSE) stream resigns suddenly. To prevent work stoppage, the RGBC's Project Manager arranges for the contractor's own TCP T3 (who holds identical academic qualifications and professional corporate membership) to concurrently sign off both the Contractor stream and the RSE stream site supervision checklists in the safety logbook.
options: A. This concurrent dual appointment is fully permissible under the Code of Practice for Site Safety Supervision (SSPS Code) because the individual satisfies the required academic and professional criteria for both streams.

B. The SSPS Code strictly prohibits cross-stream concurrent appointments; a TCP representing the contractor stream cannot concurrently act as a TCP for the AP, RSE, or RGE streams due to statutory conflict of interest.
C. Cross-stream concurrent representation is allowed for up to 14 days during emergency personnel transitions provided the AP logs the event.
D. The contractor's TCP may cover both streams only if the foundation depth is less than 15 metres below ground.
questions.statutoryRef: Code of Practice for Site Safety Supervision (SSPS Code) Section 5 & PNRC 38
questions.rationale: Under the Code of Practice for Site Safety Supervision (SSPS Code, Section 5), the separation of supervisory duties between the AP/RSE/RGE stream and the Registered Contractor (RC) stream is mandatory. A Technically Competent Person (TCP) in the Contractor's stream cannot simultaneously undertake safety supervision responsibilities for the AP/RSE stream. Doing so is an invalid supervisory appointment and a serious breach of statutory site safety supervision.
